title: Genghis Khan's Fake Army: The Fall of Samarkand (1220)
description:
In March 1220 Genghis Khan reached Samarkand, the richest city on the Silk Road. It had eight iron gates, war elephants and tens of thousands of defenders. Within weeks the city had surrendered, its garrison was executed, and the Khwarazmian Empire was finished. How did a fake army of prisoners help the Mongols, how many men really fought, and is the "2.5 million dead" number true? We compare the sources.

What would you have done in the shah's place: one big battle, or trust the walls? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for the next battle: Kulikovo 1380.

Army sizes and death tolls are disputed: medieval chroniclers often exaggerated, and modern sources disagree a lot. We show the ranges.
